first_impression.reaction: I googled 'mykonos wedding' half expecting party-island beach club stuff. Instead the intro gives me three decisions in order: legal or symbolic, season, then area and venue type. No 'say I do in paradise'. That's enough to keep me reading, and the key takeaways box is exactly what I'd paste into our shared doc.

journey.quote: A Mykonos wedding comes down to three decisions, made in order: whether the ceremony is legal or symbolic, which starts the paperwork clock; the season, read from official climate figures and current travel advice; and the area and kind of venue that suit your guest list.
journey.reaction: Good. Tell us what to decide first so we're not doing spreadsheets for 18 months.

journey.section: Choosing where to marry on Mykonos
journey.quote: Settle the kind of place first, then the name.
journey.reaction: Wait, the intro said legal or symbolic first, then season, then venue. The article then opens with venues, then weather, and the legal bit comes third. Not a big deal, but James will notice and ask which order we're actually meant to go in.

journey.section: Resorts with chapels, beach settings and private villas
journey.quote: A chapel setting tells you nothing about the legal form of the ceremony, so ask each venue whether its chapel suits a civil or a symbolic ceremony.
journey.reaction: That's an insider point. I'd have assumed a chapel meant a 'real' wedding. Exactly the kind of trap I want someone to flag for us.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: Ceremonies take place on The Ocean Balcony, just above Psarou beach, for up to 60 guests, and the wedding party can then move to the L'Archipel restaurant and pool area for up to 120.
journey.reaction: This is the most useful line for us. At 60 to 90 guests, the balcony is tight and we'd need another ceremony plan. Real numbers, not adjectives.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: The hotel describes its weddings as running from intimate gatherings to large weddings with up to 800 guests, from welcome cocktails to five-course gala dinners.
journey.reaction: Saint John fits our numbers comfortably and has a chapel. That one goes on the list for a closer look.

journey.section: Weather by month at Naxos, the nearest official weather station
journey.quote: The figures below are for Naxos, the nearest official weather station, so read them as a guide to the neighbouring Cyclades rather than a forecast for your venue.
journey.reaction: Honest. I'd rather they admit it's the next island over than pretend. James will like the table.

journey.section: Weather by month at Naxos, the nearest official weather station
journey.quote: At Naxos the prevailing wind blows from the north in every month, and the station's mean wind readings run higher from July to October than in May and June.
journey.reaction: Didn't know this. Combined with October's rain, it nudges me towards late May or June. Useful trade-off.

journey.quote: Plan water, hats, light fabrics, shade and air-conditioned rest for guests, and set a summer ceremony later in the day.
journey.reaction: Calm, practical. This block is going straight to Mum and Dad, who will worry about Nan in the heat.

journey.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness, and can be lodged by appointment at an Australian Passport Office, at many Australian embassies and consulates overseas, or by registered mail to the Authentications Section in Melbourne or Sydney; a fee applies.
journey.reaction: Skimming by here. We'll probably sign at home and do a symbolic ceremony, so I'm not sure how much of this applies to us, and nothing tells me I can skip it.

journey.quote: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but it may not work as proof of a name change.
journey.reaction: As a lawyer, I appreciate this. It's the sort of thing that bites you at the bank six months later.

journey.quote: Guests flying from Australia arrive tired, and some will be older or less steady on stairs.
journey.reaction: That's Nan. And the step-free route questions are ones I'd never have thought to ask.

journey.section: House rules to agree before you book
journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: Yes. This checklist goes into our shared doc tonight.

journey.section: Choosing where to marry on Mykonos (CTA)
journey.quote: Once you have an area and a style in mind, [talk to Wonderland Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mykonos-wedding&utm_content=primary).
journey.reaction: Mid-article it's 'Wonderland Concierge', at the end it's 'Wedded Concierge'. Are those the same service? Small, but it makes me wonder how joined-up the team is.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: Tone is right, not pushy, and 'one person' is what I want. But I'd already read 'a single point of contact, start to finish' earlier, so the second time it sounds a bit scripted.

unanswered_questions: Is there a real Mykonos wedding you've planned, with the venue and date, that we can look at?
Mykonos has a party reputation. How do we make it feel elegant rather than try-hard to our friends?
For 60 to 90 guests, which of these venues would you actually steer us towards?
Who gets older guests from the airport to the venue: the venue, Wedded Concierge, or us?
Are 'Wonderland Concierge' and 'Wedded Concierge' the same thing?
How far ahead do the popular Mykonos venues usually book out for a late May or June date?

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact, start to finish, and confirms the unpublished details above and every inclusion in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: Not pushy, but the same promise comes back almost word for word in the closing. Repeated, it reads like a script rather than a person, which makes me question how personal the service really is.

turn_offs_found.turn_off: Clichés: fairytale, dream day, say I do in paradise
turn_offs_found.quote: The sunset coast suits couples who want the light to do the work.
turn_offs_found.why: Mild, and nothing like the usual 'paradise' stuff, but it's the one line that drifts towards brochure voice in an otherwise very concrete section.

would_share_with: James (partner): the Mykonos Blu and Saint John capacity lines, plus the house rules checklist
Mum and Dad (contributing): the heat, wildfire and travel insurance block
Both sets of parents: the step-free access questions, for the grandparents

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [plan your Mykonos wedding with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mykonos-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The advice is solid and the fee agreed in writing up front is reassuring. But we haven't chosen Mykonos yet, and I'd want to read another post or two and see one real wedding before handing over our details.

top_3_changes: Make the intro's order match the article (or reorder the sections), since it promises legal, season, venue but delivers venue, season, legal.
Use one name for the concierge service throughout: the mid-article CTA says 'Wonderland Concierge' while the closing says 'Wedded Concierge'.

Say the 'one person, start to finish, confirmed in writing' promise once, either at the mid-article CTA or the closing, not both; and add a line at the top of the documents section telling couples who sign at home they can skip ahead.

open_questions.question: Real weddings, guest transfers and booking lead times are business details (deferred). Listed as unanswered questions only, not must-fix. The Wonderland/Wedded Concierge naming mismatch may be a brand-terms issue for the editor.

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'mykonos wedding' during early destination research, about 14 months out, Mykonos not yet chosen.
